candidates.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
candidates.content: Situated 3D reasoning requires embodied agents to interpret objects, scene geometry, and viewpoint dependent spatial relations. Existing methods learn grounded interactions from supervised traces, but largely imitate prescribed evidence acquisition patterns rather than optimizing the support that the returned evidence provides for the correct answer. Moreover, outcome rewards provide limited credit for intermediate tool choices and may leave infrequent tools underexplored. An effective agent should instead adaptively decide what to ground, which tool to invoke, and how to assess the utility of returned evidence. To this end, this paper presents CARE-3D, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on grounding instructions first establishes valid interactions, after which Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) optimizes the agent while keeping the 3D grounding module frozen. CARE-3D combines Counterfactual Attribution of Returned Evidence for evidence sensitive credit assignment, and Group Coverage Sampling to preserve tool coverage. candidates.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
candidates.content: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed. However, scaling human-video ICL on world-action models (WAMs) faces two challenges: task-level human-robot pairs are not temporally aligned with robot actions, and standard action losses allow policies to rely on initial-scene or task-identity shortcuts rather than tracking the context. We present Entangle, an in-context world-action model that maps a single human video and current robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. To scale temporally aligned training data, we convert recorded robot videos into matched human contexts via video-to-video generation, supplemented by real paired recordings. For model training, we combine variable-length video windows with an intra-task contrastive objective that distinguishes the paired action trajectory from other executions of the same task, preventing task-identity shortcuts. candidates.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
candidates.content: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. Across 9,136 attempts by four coding agents, the difficulty lies in stored state. Feedback that points to the first state mismatch raises acceptance over output-only feedback in all 12 agent--task cells of a matched study, by 25.0 to 46.9 percentage points, and halves the agent-hours per accepted design. candidates.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
candidates.content: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not yet available as open weights: We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening. candidates.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0
candidates.content: Release: datasette-charts 0.2a0 I introduced this new charting plugin for Datasette yesterday . Today it's gained integration with Datasette Agent , so now you can ask chat for a chart and it will create one for you using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools. Here's a demo video, recorded on agent.datasette.io where you can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin yourself: Download the video (MP4) I prompt Datasette Agent to "Use #stats to show sqlite-utils downloads over time as a chart" - where typing "#stats" opens a table search box. candidates.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
candidates.content: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted. The photo at the top of https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/technology/moltbook-ai-so... is my laptop, taken in my garden, after hunting around for the best spot that didn't have too much glare on the screen. You can see how dirty my screen is, too! Photography for a newspaper is photo journalism, and they take it seriously. (Thankfully I did not have a visible stain on my shirt.) Tags: photography , new-york-times , hacker-news , journalism

candidates.title: Blockade of PD-1 in Conjunction With the Dendritic Cell/Myeloma Vaccines Following Stem Cell Transplantation
candidates.content: [PHASE2] COMPLETED | 申办方/赞助方: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center | 适应症: Multiple Myeloma. The purpose of this research study is to determine the safety of CT-011 alone, as well as the combination of the Dendritic cell fusion vaccine and CT-011, after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT). We are also trying to find out what effect the combination has on the disease, including if it is more successful in preventing or delaying the disease from coming back, compared to treatment with autologous transplantation alone. ASCT is a standard therapy for multiple myeloma that is often successful in significantly decreasing the amount of cancer in the body. CT-011 is an investigational monoclonal antibody. Monoclonal antibodies are a type of drug given by infusion into a vein and are known to target specific cells (in this case, cells in the immune system). The dendritic cell fusion vaccine is an investigational agent that tries to help the immune system to recognize and fight against cancer cells. Unlike a standard vaccine that is used to prevent infections, cancer vaccines are being studied to see if they can fight cancers that are already in the body.

candidates.title: Impact of an HPV Primary Prevention Intervention on HPV Vaccination Rates Among Adolescents in the AuRA Region.
candidates.content: [NA] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Centre Leon Berard | 适应症: Middle School and High School Students. Human papillomaviruses (HPV) are very common contagious viruses: approximately 70% of men and women will be infected during their lifetime. Vaccination, recommended since 2007 for girls and since 2021 for all young people aged 11 to 14 (with catch-up vaccination possible up to age 26), remains insufficiently followed. Today, only 40.7% of adolescents are vaccinated in France, and the Auvergne Rhône Alpes region remains below the targets (47.5% for girls and 12.3% for boys). This is still far from the national target of 80% vaccination coverage by 2030, while 6,400 new cases of HPV-related cancers are reported each year. The PIMCOP regional study aims to assess the impact of a primary prevention intervention, co-developed with stakeholders and implemented in middle and high schools, on the HPV vaccination rate at 6 months among 11-17 year olds.

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn about the safety and efficacy of a potential new treatment called Lenti-HPV-07 in patients with a cancer induced by Human Papilloma Virus (HPV). The main questions aim to answer are: * Is Lenti-HPV-07 safe? * Does Lenti-HPV-07 induce an immune response? Participants will be assigned to a group based on their cancer type * either study drug group A: recurrent and/or metastatic cancer * or study drug group B: newly diagnosed with locally advanced cancer After they finish the study treatment, they will be followed for up to 1 year. Follow-up visits will occur via clinic visits or phone calls 4 weeks after the last study treatment and then quarterly for up to 1 year.

candidates.title: [Correspondence] The PSMAddition trial in metastatic prostate cancer – Authors’ reply
candidates.content: We appreciate the interest in the PSMAddition study.1 Paolo Zaurito and colleagues discuss the study's control arm, toxicity of the triplet, and financial implications. We acknowledge that several triplets are now proven to enhance efficacy by adding a third drug to the androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) and androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) backbone in molecularly selected patient populations.1–4 However, at the time of study design, results from docetaxel triplets were only emerging. The addition of docetaxel to the contemporary standard backbone of ADT and ARPI is of unproven benefit, and we encourage enrolment into actively accruing clinical trials specifically assessing the utility of chemotherapy for patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive prostate cancer (NCT06931340, NCT06592924).

candidates.title: [Perspectives] A fearless vulnerability
candidates.content: “I wanted to know, too, not just why people get sick, but why they suffer”, Jonathan Gleason writes in Field Guide to Falling Ill, Essays. His insights in this book come from his experience of health care as a patient, his work as an interpreter for Spanish patients in a free clinic, and his candid experiences as a gay man navigating the historical inheritance of the HIV/AIDS epidemic and the emotional and financial burden of staying safe in his relationships. In this book, he unspools the threads of how medicine and illness have shaped his familial and personal life, his stoical formative experiences and observations as a child of a family with a genetic disease, and of his inherited anxieties about ill-health.

candidates.title: Androgen stimulation rapidly reorganizes temporal 3D genome and epigenome states to trigger AR-mediated transcription in prostate cancer
candidates.content: Abstract Androgen receptor (AR)-mediated transcription drives prostate cancer progression and remains a critical therapeutic target. AR activation by androgens triggers nuclear translocation, DNA binding at AR regulatory elements (AREs), and transcription initiation. This process involves co-factors such as FOXA1, epigenetic modifications, and three-dimensional (3D) chromatin interactions. However, the temporal coordination of these events during AR-mediated transcription remains poorly understood. Using a time-course androgen stimulation model in prostate cancer cells, we first integrated temporal multi-omics data within the MOFA+/MEFISTO framework, which identified three distinct temporal factors underlying AR-mediated transcriptional dynamics, and then used higher-resolution early time-course profiling to further explore the chromatin and transcriptional context of these temporal patterns. Our combined analyses revealed that rapid AR binding at gene promoters, as early as 5 min, is crucial for initiating nascent transcription of AR target genes. candidates.title: Single-molecule quantitative analysis of mechanical stability and unfolding kinetics of intermolecular G-quadruplexes
candidates.content: Abstract Intermolecular G-quadruplexes (Inter-G4s) are implicated in long-range nucleic acid interactions, transcriptional regulation, and phase separation, yet how RNA/DNA strand composition shapes their mechanical stability and folding behavior remains poorly understood. Heterotypic RNA–DNA (R–D) Inter-G4s are particularly difficult to resolve because ensemble measurements cannot readily distinguish them from coexisting RNA–RNA (R–R) and DNA–DNA (D–D) assemblies. We developed Inter-GDP, a single-molecule platform that tethers two G-rich strands within one DNA construct, enabling repeated Inter-G4 folding and unfolding measurements. We established the platform using CSB II and two additional G4-forming sequences derived from structurally resolved bimolecular DNA G4s. Across three sequence contexts, the mean unfolding force followed the same ordering, R–R > D–D > R–D. BG4 responses were sequence- and construct-dependent, with reduced mean unfolding forces observed for Inter-G4 constructs associated with parallel bulk CD signatures. candidates.title: SHFL engages CCR4–NOT to promote CNOT3-dependent mRNA decay
candidates.content: Abstract SHFL (Shiftless) is an interferon-stimulated antiviral factor implicated in multiple modes of viral restriction, including inhibition of −1 programmed ribosomal frameshifting (−1 PRF). However, how SHFL interfaces with host post-transcriptional regulatory pathways remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that SHFL promotes mRNA turnover through the CCR4–NOT-associated 5′–3′ mRNA decay pathway. SHFL reduced the abundance of −1 PRF-containing reporters and induced mRNA decay when tethered to the 3′ untranslated region, indicating that SHFL-mediated RNA turnover can be triggered independently of the −1 PRF context. Mechanistically, SHFL interacted with endogenous CNOT3 and directly associated with the reconstituted CNOT1/2/3 NOT module in vitro . Functional analyses further showed that CNOT3 is required for efficient SHFL-mediated mRNA decay. In contrast, SHFL-mediated repression of −1 PRF-dependent translation remained intact in CNOT3 knockout cells, supporting a mechanistic separation between SHFL-mediated mRNA decay and −1 PRF translational repression. candidates.title: ATM-mediated displacement of BRD4 from damaged chromatin
candidates.content: Abstract Bromodomain-containing protein 4 (BRD4) is a chromatin reader that plays a critical role in genome maintenance. BRD4 binds to acetylated histones and acts as a scaffold to recruit various factors involved in chromatin remodeling, transcription initiation and elongation, and DNA repair. Despite BRD4’s central role in these key processes, the mechanisms that regulate its activity and dynamic interactions with chromatin are not fully understood. Using Xenopus egg extracts, we identified BRD4 as a novel substrate of the damage response kinase ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM). In response to DNA double-strand breaks, ATM rapidly phosphorylates and displaces BRD4 from acetylated histones. Displacing BRD4 from chromatin promotes histone deacetylation that modulates chromatin accessibility, DNA end processing, and repair. These findings establish a rapid, signaling-dependent mechanism for regulating BRD4 function by controlling its association with chromatin.
